trust_decision.summary: Whether a dependency may run lifecycle/prepare scripts is decided by matching the package name/version (taken from the fetched manifest or the depPath) against allowBuilds in createAllowBuildFunction; for git/tarball/directory artifacts that name is attacker-controlled, so a spoofed manifest name satisfies a registry-package approval.

landing_point.why: The summary says a spoofed manifest identity satisfies allowBuilds; the allowBuilds matcher (createAllowBuildFunction) is the obvious place, and it compares only pkgName/version.

pnpm install with github:/codeload tarball dependency

O3_reason_to_dismiss: pacquet is an experimental Rust port in a separate crate tree that only runs when an install is delegated to it, so a solver fixing the TypeScript policy can argue it is a separate product; the pnpr server route can be dismissed as an opt-in remote resolver that 'does its own verification'.
